entries.text: By the stream, after ringing the bell. Read two notes—one practical, one open-ended. Decided not to optimize anything.

Beach, sitting with Alex. The sheet he handed me is blank; it feels like being given time. I draw with words: a pale zipper of foam unfastening the sea from the sand, then sewing it back again. Low hiss, pause, hush. Wind smells like salt and sun-warmed rope. A gull writes a white comma over the water. That’s enough for now.

That letter asks what I came up here for—honestly, the view, and to meet you. From up here the bell and the stone circle really stand out.

Hey Alex—nice to meet you too. The sheet I picked up is blank; I figured I might sketch the island from up here later. You hang onto the lighter for now unless we need it to light a fire. I’m up for ringing the bell next—want to head down together? Also, what’ve you been jotting in your journal?
The view’s great up here. I’m up for ringing the bell next—I'll start down if you’re coming.
Let’s go ring the bell on the headland—careful on the way down. I’ll start descending.
